newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: OPTIONS - PHILIPS, AKZO CALL DEMAND AS SHARES GAIN.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - PHILIPS, AKZO CALL DEMAND AS SHARES GAIN.

text.p: Call options in Philips, Akzo Nobel and financials were in demand on the European Options Exchange after the Fed kept rates steady and shares soared.
"Philips has really led the way," one trader said.

Traders said short-term volatility of Akzo had risen sharply, leading to demand for October calls at 200 and 205 guilders. Philips October 60s and 62.50s traded about 3,000 contracts each. A few traders also reported interest in January calls, some for as high as 65 guilders.
Growth of financials' stocks also made call buying and put selling of ABN AMRO and of ING popular.

Outside options trade in blue-chip stocks and the index, speculation that software firm Baan had won an order from Ford Motor Company led to buying of October and November calls in the U.S. at $35, some $2-$3 above the shares' current value.
Amsterdam traders also reported dealings in guilder denominated OTC options on Baan shares. The company is listed both in Amsterdam and on Nasdaq.
